chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ahmad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibnammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdillah, from Zurarah, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man who doubted during the Adhan, but had already entered the Iqamah.' He said, 'He continues.' I said: 'A man who doubted both the Adhan and the Iqamah, and had already said Takbir.' He said, 'He continues.' I said: 'He doubted the Takbir, but had already recited.' He said, 'He continues.' I said: 'He doubted the recitation, but had already bowed.' He said, 'He continues.' I said: 'He doubted the bowing, but had already prostrated.' He said, 'He continues in his prayer.' Then he said: 'O Zurarah, when you exit one matter and enter another, your doubt is of no consequence.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on prayer if one doubts a previous step but has already performed the next step?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes the principle of 'istishab' (presumption of continuity) in Shia jurisprudence, where doubt in a prior pillar is disregarded once the worshipper has firmly entered the subsequent stage of prayer. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that uncertainty is only valid if it arises within the current component; once one transitions to a new act, the previous doubt is nullified. This ruling minimizes disruption in worship by preventing excessive doubt (waswasa) from invalidating prayers based on minor uncertainties in earlier steps.
